issues.description: ALTER TABLE no longer accepts multiple comma-delimited table options in a single statement
issues.detail: The outer Delimited wrapper around the OneOf was removed and replaced with a bare OneOf. Previously sequences like 'ALTER TABLE t SET (...), SET (...)' or multiple table options at top level could parse; now only a single clause per ALTER TABLE is allowed. This is a behavioral regression in addition to the intended fix for DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar permits a sign token on the increment, allowing syntactically invalid IDENTITY(-1, -)
issues.detail: Adding SignedSegmentGrammar before both numeric literals is too permissive: T-SQL IDENTITY accepts a negative seed but the increment is always a positive integer per docs. Consider restricting the sign to the seed only, or validating that the sign is followed by a numeric literal in both positions without standalone signs.

issues.description: DEFAULT_DATABASE/DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accept any NakedIdentifier including reserved words
issues.detail: Using NakedIdentifierSegment for DEFAULT_DATABASE and DEFAULT_LANGUAGE values is convenient but allows tokens that wouldn't be valid database/language identifiers. Also DEFAULT_LANGUAGE now accepts NumericLiteralSegment with no test coverage for that branch. Add fixtures for the numeric case or remove it.

issues.description: Missing test for CREATE LOGIN with DEFAULT_LANGUAGE as numeric literal
issues.detail: The grammar now allows DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = <number> but no test fixture exercises that branch. Either add a test case demonstrating the numeric form (e.g. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE = 1033) or remove that OneOf alternative to keep the grammar minimal.

issues.description: Missing test fixture for nested DECLARE @t TABLE (... INDEX ...) with multi-column index
issues.detail: The new TableIndexSegment ref in DeclareStatementSegment is exercised only with a trivial single-column index. Earlier in the fixture file an inline 'index _name (name)' style appears on a column; add a multi-column standalone INDEX line to ensure parity with CREATE TABLE index syntax and prevent regressions.

issues.description: declare_table_type.sql test case omits trailing semicolon and uses inconsistent casing
issues.detail: The new statement at the end of the file lacks a terminating semicolon while every other statement in the file has one, and mixes lowercase 'declare ... table' with the uppercase style used above. Minor consistency issue that makes the fixture less canonical.

review.summary: The PR adds useful TSQL parser coverage (table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, negative IDENTITY seeds, multi-DROP COLUMN/CONSTRAINT) with reasonable fixtures. The most notable concern is the AlterTableStatementSegment refactor: removing the outer Delimited wrapper changes the statement from accepting multiple comma-separated alterations to a single clause per statement, which is a regression beyond the stated scope (the removed test case is evidence). Minor concerns: IdentityGrammar over-accepts signed increments, DEFAULT_LANGUAGE numeric branch is untested, and the new declare fixture is stylistically inconsistent.
